
{{alias}}( N, x, strideX, sum, count )
    Computes the sum of single-precision floating-point strided array elements,
    ignoring `NaN` values, using an improved Kahan–Babuška algorithm, and
    returns the number of non-`NaN` elements.

    The `N` and stride parameters determine which elements in the strided array
    are accessed at runtime.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use a typed
    array view.

    If `N <= 0`, the function sets `sum` to `0.0` and `count` to `0`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    x: Float32Array
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length for `x`.

    sum: Float32Array
        Output array for storing the sum.

    count: Int32Array
        Output array for storing the number of non-NaN elements.

    Returns
    -------
    sum: Float32Array
        Output array containing the sum.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard Usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, NaN, 2.0 ] );
    > var sum = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( 1 );
    > var count = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}( x.length, x, 1, sum, count )
    <Float32Array>[ 1.0 ]
    > count[ 0 ]
    3

    // Using `N` and stride parameters:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( [ -2.0, 1.0, 1.0, -5.0, 2.0, -1.0, NaN, NaN ] );
    > sum = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( 1 );
    > count = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}( 4, x, 2, sum, count )
    <Float32Array>[ 1.0 ]

    // Using view offsets:
    > var x0 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, 2.0, 5.0, 1.0, NaN, NaN ] );
    > var x1 = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( x0.buffer, x0.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT*1 );
    > sum = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( 1 );
    > count = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}( 4, x1, 2, sum, count )
    <Float32Array>[ 1.0 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, sum, offsetSum, count, offsetCount )
    Computes the sum of single-precision floating-point strided array elements,
    ignoring `NaN` values, using an improved Kahan–Babuška algorithm and
    alternative indexing semantics, and returns the number of non-`NaN`
    elements.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameters support indexing semantics based on starting
    indices.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    x: Float32Array
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length for `x`.

    offsetX: integer
        Starting index for `x`.

    sum: Float32Array
        Output array for storing the sum.

    offsetSum: integer
        Starting index for `sum`.

    count: Int32Array
        Output array for storing the number of non-NaN elements.

    offsetCount: integer
        Starting index for `count`.

    Returns
    -------
    sum: Float32Array
        Output array containing the sum.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard Usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, NaN, 2.0 ] );
    > var sum = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( 1 );
    > var count = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( x.length, x, 1, 0, sum, 0, count, 0 )
    <Float32Array>[ 1.0 ]

    // Using offset parameter:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, 2.0, 5.0, 1.0, NaN, NaN ] );
    > sum = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float32}}( 1 );
    > count = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 4, x, 2, 1, sum, 0, count, 0 )
    <Float32Array>[ 1.0 ]

    See Also
    --------
